sources.entry: Anubis - Web AI firewall utility which protects upstream resources from scraper bots. (Source Code) MIT Docker/deb/Go

summary.one_liner: Anubis is a self-hosted Web AI Firewall utility that puts challenges in front of web traffic to block scraper bots from upstream resources.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Anubis as a Web AI Firewall Utility that applies one or more challenges to incoming connections to protect upstream resources from scraper bots. It is positioned as a lightweight option for sites that cannot or will not use Cloudflare. Bot policy definitions can be configured to explicitly allowlist specific bots, such as the Internet Archive. The README says a curated set of "known good" bots is being worked on. Documentation is hosted on a separate site (anubis.techaro.lol), and the README points to an issue tracker for support. Beyond these points, the README gives no detailed feature list.
use_cases: protect a website from AI scraper bots
block aggressive crawlers on a small site
allowlist good bots like the Internet Archive
rate-limit or challenge suspicious web traffic
how_to_run: See the documentation site at anubis.techaro.lol for installation and setup instructions
notable: Challenge-based firewall that weighs connections rather than simply blocking by IP
Bot policy definitions allow explicit allowlisting of specific crawlers
Designed to be lightweight so small operators can afford to run it
Works as an alternative when Cloudflare cannot be used
caveats: The README calls it a 'nuclear response' that will block smaller scrapers and may also block good bots like the Internet Archive unless configured
Live chat support requires joining a Patreon
Setup details are not in the README and must be found on the external documentation site
